title: Long-term development of a motor memory
abstract: Abstract Human behaviour is developed through continuous adaptation to our environment over a range of timescales. Extensive studies have investigated the mechanisms and computations underlying this process of sensorimotor adaptation using several hundred trials. However, most of our motor skills have had countless hours of practice. Here we study a simple motor adaptation task using thousands of training trials over multiple weeks to study the long-term development of a motor memory, and examine changes in adaptation, retention, interlimb transfer, decay, spontaneous recovery and generalization. Unlike previous studies, participants showed near complete compensation to the novel dynamics, along with long-term increases in retention and spontaneous recovery. Moreover, we find narrowing in the angular generalization, suggesting continual tuning of the motor memory to the task. This demonstrates the extensive changes occurring with longer training of motor tasks, highlighting their importance in studies of sensorimotor control, rehabilitation and training.
abstract_zh: 人类行为通过在各种时间尺度上持续适应环境而形成。大量研究利用数百次试验，探究了感知运动适应背后的机制和计算过程。然而，我们大多数的运动技能都经历了数小时的练习。本研究利用数周内数千次训练试验，研究运动记忆的长期发展，并检验适应、保留、双侧迁移、衰减、自发恢复和外推泛化的变化。与以往研究不同，参与者对新动力学表现出近乎完全的补偿，且保留和自发恢复呈长期增加。此外，我们发现角度外推泛化范围的收窄，表明运动记忆持续针对任务进行调整。这展示了在更长时间运动任务训练中发生的广泛变化，突显了它们在感知运动控制、康复和训练研究中的重要性。
